claims.text: A high density of coherent, hierarchical nanoprecipitates governs high-temperature plastic strain in refractory high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys.
A high density of coherent, hierarchical nanoprecipitates governs toughness in these refractory alloys.
The relevant initial state is a single-phase refractory solid solution without significant incoherent precipitates.
A controlled processing route can produce stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Varying precipitate coherence or volume fraction while retaining a similar alloy composition provides a controlled comparison that isolates the precipitate effect.
Deformation at 600–800 °C is representative of plasma-facing component conditions.
Diffusion-controlled precipitate coarsening is minimized during the proposed 600–800 °C tests.
The nanoprecipitate interfaces are coherent, stable, and well bonded to the matrix.
Coherent nanoprecipitates hinder dislocation motion and thereby increase yield strength.
Coherent nanoprecipitates promote sustained strain hardening.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Dislocation transmission through coherent interfaces relieves stress concentrations and delays premature crack initiation.
The coherent-nanoprecipitate alloy will have higher yield strength at high temperature than the precipitate-free or incoherent-phase baseline.
The coherent-nanoprecipitate alloy will retain more plastic strain at high temperature than the baseline.
The coherent-nanoprecipitate alloy will have greater fracture toughness than the baseline.
Incoherent secondary phases do not promote dislocation transfer and can degrade plastic performance.
The proposed mechanism remains applicable up to approximately 1000 °C if precipitate coarsening remains minimal.
Diffusion-driven transformations can override the proposed precipitate-mediated deformation mechanism during hot deformation.
The quantitative mechanical improvements depend on alloy system, precipitate size, precipitate volume fraction, and processing parameters.

Failure to obtain reproducible, statistically significant gains in yield strength, strain hardening, and fracture toughness, or failure to observe altered dislocation transfer, would falsify the proposed mechanism.
